| [ADR-068](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-068.md) v2 | Reading and filing follow a written protocol: its invariants are held in this decision, and its steps in a skill that changes with practice | The record takes in reading through a practice of eleven steps: intake, a check against the record, identifiers, registration, a lawful copy, reading, verification, filing the reading, filing the argument, accounting for everything, and acknowledgement. Until now it lived in session memory and in the pieces [ADR-002](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-002.md), [ADR-008](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-008.md), [ADR-041](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-041.md), [ADR-053](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-053.md), [ADR-054](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-054.md), [ADR-064](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-064.md) and [ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md) decided one at a time. Each session rebuilt it, and applied it unevenly ([ADR-064](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-064.md)'s case). This decision fixes the eight invariants. The steps go in `.claude/skills/read-and-file/SKILL.md`, edited in the pull request whose work shows a step wrong. Rejected: leaving the practice unwritten; writing every step into an ADR, which would make each refinement a supersession; a section of CLAUDE.md, which is a map and not a manual; a page under docs/, which is generated; and building it into luria before the steps have settled. | Proposed |
| [ADR-075](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-075.md) v4 | A synthesis in a filed source is audited and, when it integrates, filed as a thesis claim with its components mapped, rather than mapped to its source turns and left | Filing has treated a source's syntheses (executive summaries, positive accounts, recaps, "refreshed syntheses") as recaps: each item is mapped to the turn it came from, and the synthesis is left. That finds new content but leaves the integration with no address. So the record can't say what its current account is, and later syntheses can't be checked for drift. The exchange "Individuation, Possibility, and Disposition" produced four summaries of the record's account. They recast the owner's prompts as the argument's own logic and dropped two of the owner's contributions, and nothing on the record could catch it. This decision adds a synthesis audit to the read-and-file skill: find every synthesis, group its versions, classify it as descriptive, supposed or proposed, map its components to codes, and check attribution, coverage, fidelity, standing and integration. The latest version of each distinct proposed or supposed thesis is filed as one CLAIM, with its components in `rests_on` or the body, and revised in place when it returns. A synthesis is admitted as an independent hypothesis, a derived result or an explanatory integration, each with its own test (versions 2 and 3). Rejected: a new scheme for positions, until a synthesis CLAIM strains; filing every version; and the status quo. | Proposed |
| [ADR-076](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-076.md) v3 | Syntheses get a scheme of their own, SYNTHESIS, with statuses about the integration, a closed admission route, components whose standing is derived, and a generated current-account view | A synthesis filed as a CLAIM strains the CLAIM scheme four ways. Its components' voice and standing live in prose and drift. Its admission route has no field. CLAIM's status vocabulary has no word for "exhausted by its components", so the first synthesis that failed admission was marked Rejected, which says false. And nothing renders the record's current account, which the owner wants. This decision adds a SYNTHESIS scheme. It keeps three judgements apart: a status for the integrating account (Current, Proposed, Rejected, Superseded); an `admission` field (admitted or unadmitted), saying whether it earned an entry; and relations for its components. It has a closed `route`, required while admitted,: hypothesis, derived or integration. It has `integrates` and `premises` relations, whose targets' standing a generated view derives. The view, docs/current-account.md, is a Jinja template that sets out every Current or Proposed synthesis by line, with each component's status read from the component when the page is built. The five syntheses filed from "Individuation, Possibility, and Disposition" are moved into it as the demonstration, and their CLAIMs are Superseded by the new entries. ARG's `concludes` accepts a synthesis. Rejected: a route field on CLAIM; a CLAIM-only status vocabulary; DP's document rendering; the status quo. | Proposed |
| [ADR-077](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-077.md) | A claim moved into the SYNTHESIS scheme keeps its standing and its relations: an admitted Active claim becomes a Current synthesis, and the scheme gains grounds, uses and corroborated_by so that nothing is dropped | The first synthesis review admitted [CLAIM-474](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-474.md) and could not move it. A review files every synthesis as Proposed, so an Active claim would have been demoted, and SYNTHESIS lacked grounds, uses and corroborated_by, so moving it would have dropped its readings, terms and corroboration. This decision amends [ADR-076](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-076.md) and the review's decision. A move keeps the claim's standing: an admitted Active CLAIM becomes a Current SYNTHESIS and a Proposed one stays Proposed, since the move changes the scheme that holds the entry, not the record's credence in it. The scheme gains the three fields, with their converses widened to match. A review still never sets a new synthesis Current. Its demonstration is [CLAIM-474](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-474.md)'s move. Rejected: moving as Proposed and asking for re-adoption; exempting adopted claims from the move; the owner setting each moved synthesis Current by hand. | Proposed |
| [ADR-078](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-078.md) | The record is reviewed periodically for synthesis opportunities: CLAIMs that are syntheses filed as claims are moved into the SYNTHESIS scheme, and integrations whose parts the record holds are filed when they pass admission | [ADR-075](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-075.md) audits the syntheses a source brings, and [ADR-076](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-076.md) gives them a scheme and a current-account view. Neither looks at what the record already holds. Some CLAIMs are syntheses filed before the scheme existed, [CLAIM-545](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-545.md) among them. Some integrations sit in the record as parts, such as `complements` clusters, questions with several answers and deep chains, that no entry states. This decision adds a periodic synthesis review, carried by the `synthesis-review` skill. Its first stage is mechanical: scratch/formal/synthesis_candidates.py ranks candidates in two arms, migration and opportunity, and decides nothing. A reviewer then shortlists a dozen at most, preferring in-force components and lines the current-account view does not cover. Each is audited with [ADR-075](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-075.md)'s five checks and admitted by one of its three routes or not at all. An admitted migration moves into the scheme, with its relations audited. An admitted opportunity is filed as a Proposed SYNTHESIS in the assistant's voice. Nothing is set Current, and what is not admitted is recorded with its reason. Rejected: reviewing only at filing time; filing every candidate the ranking finds; leaving the sweep ad hoc. | Proposed |
